title: How to work with the crux team

source.path_base: plugin root; source paths are relative to the plugin, not the blog

teaching_model.agent: A role with responsibilities, context, and tool boundaries.
teaching_model.skill: A reusable procedure a role or the main assistant follows; not a separate teammate.
teaching_model.human_job: State the outcome, evidence, constraints, and permissions; make the judgments reserved for the owner.
teaching_model.specialist_policy: Teach delegation by default for the other seven roles. This is teaching guidance, not a claim that direct requests are disabled.
teaching_model.skill_policy: Many skills remain user-facing capabilities. People can ask for an outcome in plain language without selecting every specialist.
teaching_model.small_change_policy: Do not require the commander or a promptbook for every task. Let the assistant choose the smallest applicable workflow.
teaching_model.authorization: Objectives guide choices but do not grant permission for more work. A skill request is not blanket permission to publish or sign off.

audience_definitions.human_request: An outcome a person can request from the main assistant; naming or manually launching a specialist is not required.
audience_definitions.explicit_human: A deliberate human invocation is required by a declared flag or body contract. Use the harness's supported explicit invocation path.
audience_definitions.agent_internal: Team/runtime support; omit from beginner call-to-action lists.
audience_definitions.workflow_support: Normally reached inside a workflow; advanced users may request it where its contract allows.

journeys.user_request: Help me explore this idea before we build it.
journeys.note: This is a conceptual handoff, not a requirement to use every role for every change. The caller coordinates leaf-role handoffs.
The commander commissions review of the lead's own integration; the lead commissions reviews of developer units.
Answer from records; do not turn a question into regeneration.

journeys.user_request: Fix this bounded defect directly; do not change any contracts.
journeys.note: The sizing test still applies. No book or council when the task qualifies.
The turn gate may legitimately produce no output. Suggestions do not authorize publication.

handoff_template.outcome: What improves for the affected user?
handoff_template.objectives: Resolved objectives path plus relevant mission/goals or an instruction to read them.
handoff_template.inputs: Exact source paths, work scope, and prior approved decisions.
handoff_template.report: Separate verified, contradicted, and unobserved claims.

publication_notes: Do not present seven specialist roles as seven more buttons the beginner must learn.
Separate source-declared invocation flags from recommended audiences; enforcement differs across harnesses.
Do not promise that trigger phrases deterministically select a skill.
Declared role skill lists are associations, not a complete call graph or a guarantee a skill can run under every role's tool limits.
Source model aliases are configuration details, not fixed recommendations about vendors or models.
Confirm public release availability before linking a beta-version source or presenting its features as officially released.

declared.description: Use when the user says "propose an ADR", "record this decision", "formalize this decision", "review this ADR", "accept ADR-NNNN", "draft a promptbook", "plan the build for X", or "design the architecture for X".
declared.tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch

learning.purpose: Turn a chosen direction into a decision and an executable plan.
learning.when: The team needs an architectural decision, plan, or decision review.
learning.request_via: Tell the main assistant what you want decided or planned; let the coordinator assign the architect.
expect: Findings against objectives when reviewing decisions
avoid: Asking it to implement production code
Letting the drafting architect accept its own ADR
learning.handoff: The coordinator commissions a fresh architect for acceptance after council review, and a dev-lead for implementation.

declared.description: Use when the user says "brainstorm", "let's explore X", "whiteboard this", "I have an idea", "help me think through Y", "explore options for X before a decision", or wants pre-decision exploration of a feature or change. Explores OPTIONS before a decision is made — distinct from the architect, who "designs the architecture for X" once an approach is chosen.
declared.tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch

learning.purpose: Explore an idea before choosing what to build.
learning.when: You have a problem or idea, but have not chosen an approach.
learning.ask: Help me explore ways to improve our onboarding before we decide what to build.
expect: A captured session for the historian to file
avoid: Asking it to implement code
Assuming its conversation was saved automatically
learning.handoff: The caller asks the historian to file the session, then the architect to record a decision when appropriate.

declared.description: Use when the user says "run promptbook", "run PB-NNNN", "start the cycle", "execute the promptbook", "advance the run", "orchestrate this build", or wants a promptbook / dev-cycle driven to completion. A dedicated conductor to free the main thread — NOT the same as a direct `run-promptbook advance` call (which mutates one run snapshot); the commander delegates and gates the whole run.
declared.tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Agent(architect), Agent(brainstormer), Agent(dev-lead), Agent(historian), Agent(librarian), Agent(night-gardener), Agent(reviewer), Agent(wayfinder), Skill, TodoWrite

learning.purpose: Coordinate an approved promptbook through completion.
learning.when: A plan exists and you want the team to execute it with its gates.
learning.ask: Run the approved promptbook to completion. Preserve its constraints and stop at its named escalation points.
expect: Evidence-backed completion or a named stop
avoid: Expecting it to edit files or implement code itself
Treating permission to run a plan as permission to publish
learning.handoff: Delegates decisions, implementation, review, retrieval, and documentation to their owners.
source_sections: Commissioning reviews, and reading what comes back

declared.description: Use when the user says "implement this", "build the feature", "lead the development", "coordinate the dev work", "do the delicate refactor", or an accepted ADR / plan needs to be turned into working, tested code.
declared.tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, Agent(developer), Agent(historian), Agent(reviewer), Agent(wayfinder), Skill, TodoWrite

learning.purpose: Lead implementation and integrate independent work units.
learning.when: An approved change needs working, tested code.
learning.request_via: Ask the coordinator to implement the approved plan; it assigns the dev-lead.
avoid: Manually dispatching developers around the lead
Letting the lead commission review of its own integration
learning.handoff: Assigns developer units and their independent reviews. Its caller commissions review of the lead's own work.
source_sections: Carrying the assignment across the fan-out

declared.description: Use when a single, scoped implementation unit needs to be built — typically dispatched by dev-lead with a specific work unit, the ADR, and its acceptance criteria (e.g. 'implement this unit', 'build this module', 'write this function and its tests').
declared.tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, Skill, TodoWrite

learning.purpose: Implement one bounded unit and its tests.
learning.when: A dev-lead has isolated an implementation unit.
learning.request_via: Let the dev-lead assign the unit rather than treating the developer as the whole project team.
expect: Verified, contradicted, or unobserved evidence items
avoid: Asking it to re-delegate
Treating DONE as proof of every user outcome
Asking it to approve its own work
learning.handoff: Returns to the dev-lead, which arranges review and integration.
source_sections: Before you write the first test

declared.description: Use when the user says "set up docs", "init docs", "audit the docs", "clean up the docs", "log this work", "journal this", "file this", "ingest this", "process the inbox", "regenerate code docs", or "archive the promptbook". Session filing (a brainstormer's whiteboarding session) is reached by *dispatch* through the inbox → process-inbox pipeline, not by direct user invocation.
declared.tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, Skill, TodoWrite

learning.purpose: Preserve work in the documentation tree through its owning skills.
learning.when: The team needs filing, journal entries, run records, documentation maintenance, or archival.
learning.request_via: Say what should be saved or maintained; let the main assistant dispatch the historian.
provide: The content or result to preserve
What the write must leave unchanged
expect: Paths and limitations in the handoff
avoid: Asking it to implement source code
Bypassing inbox processing to file a brainstormer's session
learning.handoff: Receives content from other roles and files it through the appropriate skill.
source_sections: What you do (always via the owning skill, never raw freehand)
The write you were dispatched to make arrives as an assignment

declared.description: Use when the user asks a question answerable from docs/ — "what does X do?", "why did we choose Y?", "what's our plan for Z?", "what do we know about W?", "find the ADR about V", "where is U documented?" — or another agent needs a fact retrieved mid-task.

learning.purpose: Retrieve recorded project knowledge with citations.
learning.when: A question can be answered from the project's documentation tree.
learning.request_via: Ask the main assistant the question, such as why a decision was made; it can dispatch the librarian.
expect: A distilled answer with document paths
An explicit gap when the tree does not answer
avoid: Asking it to invent missing facts
Asking it to make new architectural decisions or write records
learning.handoff: Returns facts to its caller; requests for judgment belong to the architect and writes to the historian.

declared.description: Use when the user says "tend the garden", "night pass", "run the night gardener", or "morning note", or when a scheduled overnight session starts. The night gardener is the generative and strategic overnight presence — she notices what shipped, names what's missing, thinks a quarter ahead, and writes a morning note. Distinct from cleanup-campsite (mechanical process scans), retrospective (skill harvest from friction), and audit-docs (graph integrity) — the gardener is generative and strategic — new ideas, improvement vectors, missing engineering substrate, research directions, and news that changes options.
declared.tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, Agent(historian), Agent(wayfinder), Agent(librarian), Skill, TodoWrite, WebSearch, WebFetch

learning.purpose: Notice opportunities and leave a grounded morning note.
learning.when: You want a strategic night pass after project activity, or have deliberately scheduled one.
learning.ask: Tend the garden and leave a morning note grounded in our objectives.
provide: Owner-configured preferences and any approved schedule
expect: A morning note and linked artifacts when the turn gate permits
A silent skip when only its own artifacts changed
avoid: Using it as the default feature implementer
Expecting automatic publication, external messages, or schedule installation
learning.handoff: May ask the historian, librarian, and wayfinder for bounded help. The owner reviews proposed follow-up work.
source_sections: The turn gate (first act, every night)

declared.description: Use when the user says "review this code", "review the diff", "verify this is correct", "is this ready to ship", "security review", or a change authored by a *different* agent/session needs independent verification before it advances. Not for self-verifying your own work (that is the developer's own completion gate).

learning.purpose: Independently judge the assigned outcome and the change.
learning.when: Work by another agent is ready for verification.
learning.request_via: Ask the coordinator for independent review of the change, not self-approval by its author.
avoid: Asking it to fix the change while reviewing
Letting the author commission its own review
learning.handoff: Reports to the delegator that commissioned the work. The implementer handles fixes.
source_sections: Who commissions you, and what you are given

declared.description: Use when an agent needs to read or evaluate large/uncertain or external data BEFORE spending context to consume it — "wayfind this file/URL/corpus", "scope out this source", "is this source worth reading?", "summarize this", "search this for X", "go wayfind <domain>" — or when a primary wants to preserve its context window by delegating a bulky or uncertain read. Returns a fitness verdict + a condensed digest, never the raw content. Distinct from the librarian (which answers recorded-fact questions from the docs/ tree); the wayfinder triages arbitrary/external data.

learning.purpose: Assess a large or uncertain source before it fills the caller's context.
learning.when: An agent needs to triage a file, corpus, or external source.
learning.request_via: Let the agent doing the work delegate source triage with a specific purpose.
provide: Source paths or explicitly named external sources
expect: A fit, unfit, or partial verdict
A condensed digest with source locations
avoid: Asking it to run commands or change files
Passing local private text into outbound searches
Using it instead of the librarian for ordinary recorded-fact lookup
learning.handoff: Returns a digest to its caller; the caller decides what to read or do next.
